info.title: ldapium management API
info.summary: HTTP API behind the ldapium web console, usable by scripts and AI agents with a session cookie.
info.description:
Authentication is a signed session cookie (`ldapium_session`) obtained from POST /api/login (LDAP mode) or the browser OIDC flow (SSO mode). There are no API tokens, no CORS headers and no machine principal yet; see docs/api.md and docs/changes/api-integration/PLAN.md.

Every error (4xx/5xx, including unknown paths and wrong methods) is one JSON body, the `Error` schema: `{"error", "message", "code", "requestId", "retryable"}`. `error` and `message` carry the same text (`message` is a deprecated alias); branch on `code`. 5xx text is fixed and never includes internal detail; use `requestId` to find the cause in the server log. 429 and retryable 503 responses carry `Retry-After`. The exceptions are `GET /api/health/ldap` (probe body `{"reachable": bool}`), redirects, and responses without a body (`OPTIONS` 204, `HEAD`).

Conditional writes use `ETag`/`If-Match` with quoted integer revisions (profiles, methods, backups), a quoted 64-hex fingerprint (Keycloak role operations), or, for users, groups and entry moves, the entry's quoted entryCSN (`etag` field / `ETag` header; opt-in, enforced atomically by the directory, covering attributes written directly to the entry). Profile, method, backup and Keycloak write endpoints also enforce a same-origin `Origin` header and `Content-Type: application/json`.

Safety: `userPassword` is never returned by any endpoint. Operations marked destructive are not reversible. Directory writes run as the logged-in identity (LDAP mode) or the configured service account (SSO mode) under that identity's LDAP ACLs.

get.description: Public discovery document. Reveals only what /api/auth/config reveals plus build version and which optional features are enabled.
Public, cached for 5 minutes. Served from the binary, so it always matches the running build.
Used by the SPA and by the readiness probe; never touches LDAP.
Boolean only; the reason for a failure is never returned.

post.description: Binds to the directory as the given identity (full DN or bare uid) and sets the signed session cookie `ldapium_session` (HttpOnly, SameSite=Lax). Failed attempts are rate-limited per client IP. Disabled (404) when the server runs in SSO mode.

post.description: Always ends the local session and clears the cookie; no session is required. Returns 204 in LDAP mode. In SSO mode returns 200 with the IdP logout URL the browser should visit.

get.description: All attributes of `dn`. `userPassword` is removed server-side (hard denylist), not left to directory ACLs. The revision is returned only in the `ETag` header, never in the body. The ETag covers only attributes written directly to this entry: `memberOf` and the removal of a deleted member from a group's `member` (refint) do NOT change it, so the same ETag can be returned for a different representation; re-read those attributes when they matter.

ETag.description: Strong ETag of the entry (its entryCSN, quoted). Omitted when the bound identity cannot read entryCSN. Send it back as `If-Match` on writes. It also changes on directory-side bookkeeping writes to the entry (failed/successful binds under the password policy, optional lastbind), which can cause a harmless 412 and a re-read.

post.description: Moves `dn` under `newParentDn`. 400 if the move would cross naming contexts; 409 if an entry with the same RDN already exists under `newParentDn`. OpenLDAP's mdb backend renames a non-leaf entry together with its subtree (verified live: 204), so children do not cause a 409 there. In SSO mode runs as the service account. Conditional: send `If-Match` (the target entry's `etag`) to make it atomic against concurrent edits; see the parameter.

parameters.name: If-Match
parameters.description: Optional optimistic-concurrency condition. Send the `etag` field of the list item or the `ETag` header of `GET /api/entry` exactly as received (a quoted strong tag). The write is applied only if the entry still has that revision, evaluated by the directory inside the write itself (LDAP assertion control), so a concurrent change cannot slip in; otherwise 412 `revision_conflict` and nothing is written. `*` and an absent header mean unconditional (today's behaviour). A weak tag, a list of tags, an unquoted or malformed value, or a repeated header is 400. The tag covers only attributes written directly to the entry (see GET /api/entry). Node-local: against a multi-provider replicated directory the condition is evaluated on the node that receives the write only.

get.description: ppolicy entries under the base DN.

403.description: Permission denied by directory ACL

get.description: Users under the base DN. Without `limit`, `cursor`, `q` or `sort` this is the legacy listing: at most 5000 entries in directory order, `truncated: true` when more exist. With any of those parameters the listing is paged (keyset): entries come in strictly increasing order of (lowercased smallest `uid`, lowercased DN), up to `limit` per page; follow `nextCursor` while `hasMore` is true. A page can be shorter than `limit`, even empty, while `hasMore` is true (entries can change while a page is assembled): continue on `hasMore`, never on page length. Cursors are opaque, bound to the login session (a new login invalidates them), to the resource and to the `q` they were issued with (send the same `q` on every page). Concurrent changes (no snapshot): an entry that exists and keeps its sort key and DN for the whole traversal is returned exactly once; an entry added after the cursor position may appear, one added at or before it will not; an entry deleted before its page is read is not returned, one already returned stays returned; a renamed entry or one whose sort key changed can appear twice (moved from before to after the cursor) or not at all (moved from after to before). Every page scans the whole candidate set (O(N) per page, O(N^2/limit) for a full traversal), bounded by 100000 candidates and a 30 s request deadline. The directory's size limit (olcSizeLimit, default 10000, counted over the whole scan) stops a non-admin identity with 422 `size_limit_exceeded` instead of returning a partial page: narrow with `q`, use an identity exempt from the limit (the admin DN), or ask the operator to set LDAP_PAGED_TOTAL_LIMIT (chart value ldap.limits.pagedTotal). Paged items carry the same `etag` as the legacy list and as `GET /api/entry`, usable as `If-Match`.

400.description: `cursor_invalid`: the cursor was tampered with, truncated, of an unknown version, or issued for another login session, resource or `q`. The message never says which.

422.description: `validation_failed` (limit, q or sort rejected; the message names only the field), `size_limit_exceeded` (the directory's size limit stopped the scan; no partial page) or `scan_limit_exceeded` (more than 100000 candidates; narrow with q).

503.description: `scan_timeout` (the 30 s request deadline ran out; narrow with q) or `unavailable` (another listing on the same login session held the scan slot until this request's deadline). Both are retryable and set `Retry-After` (30 s for `scan_timeout`, 2 s for `unavailable`).

403.description: Permission denied by directory ACL

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Page size, 1-200 (default 50). Sending any of limit, cursor, q or sort selects the paged mode.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: Opaque cursor: the `nextCursor` of the previous page. Invalid, tampered or foreign (other login session, resource or `q`) cursors are 400 `cursor_invalid`.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: Substring filter, at most 64 characters, valid UTF-8, no control characters; surrounding whitespace is trimmed. Matched case-insensitively against uid, cn, mail and displayName. Filter characters such as `*`, `(`, `)` and `\` are matched literally.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: Only the default key is accepted: `uid` (ascending). Any other value is 422 `validation_failed`.

post.description: Creates under LDAP_USER_CREATE_BASE. `uid` is required. If `password` is omitted none is set. With a password this is two directory operations (Add, then Password Modify). Before the password step the new entry is verified as created by this request and untouched (entryUUID/entryCSN, creator and modifier are the bound DN, modify time equals create time); otherwise the password is NOT set and nothing is deleted (`partial_failure`, `state: identity_changed`). If the password step fails the entry is removed again with a delete bound to that identity and the response is the usual error envelope whose text starts "user not created" (nothing remains). If it cannot be removed the response is 500 `partial_failure` with the `dn` and `state` `partial` (delete refused, entry remains), `unknown` (delete outcome not observed) or `identity_changed`. Password status is never guaranteed on a `partial_failure`; inspect the entry, then set the password with POST /api/users/password or DELETE it. A few milliseconds before the Password Modify remain racy: that operation cannot carry a condition.

500.description: Unexpected failure (`internal`, fixed text), or `partial_failure`: the user creation did not complete and the new entry was not removed as verified (`state`, `dn`, `retryable: false`).

MethodNotAllowed.description: Wrong method for the path (`method_not_allowed`); an `Allow` header lists the right ones.

Error.description: The one error body every /api error uses (except the GET /api/health/ldap probe, redirects and bodiless OPTIONS/HEAD responses). `error` is the primary field; `message` is an identical, deprecated alias kept for older clients. Branch on `code`, not on the text. Exception: `partial_failure` (500, POST /api/users) additionally carries `state` and `dn`; `backup_busy` (409, POST /api/v1/backups/jobs/{kind}) additionally carries `active_job_id` and `active_kind`.

error.description: Human-readable text. 4xx: the handler's curated text. 5xx: a fixed per-code text, never an internal detail.

code.description: Stable machine-readable code. The set is append-only: new codes may appear, names never change. Treat an unknown value like the status code's class default.

requestId.description: Matches the X-Request-Id response header and the server log line holding the unredacted cause.

retryable.description: Whether sending the same request again, unchanged, may succeed. False for 412/428 (reload first) and 500 (partial effects possible).

state.description: Only with `code: partial_failure` (a user creation whose password step did not complete): `partial` the verified delete was refused and the entry remains; `unknown` the delete's outcome was not observed; `identity_changed` the new entry could not be verified as created by this request and untouched, the password was NOT set and nothing was deleted. This and `dn` are the documented exception to the five-key envelope.

dn.description: Only with `code: partial_failure`: the DN of the entry to check (the value a 201 would have returned). The one DN an error body carries.

active_job_id.description: Only on `backup_busy`: the job that holds the single run slot. It can be looked up with GET /api/v1/backups/jobs/{id}; it does not prove the job is yours.

active_kind.description: Only on `backup_busy`: the kind of the running job.

UserPatchRequest.description: JSON Merge Patch (RFC 7396) for a user. A key that is absent keeps its current value; a non-empty string sets it; `null` removes it. An empty string is rejected (400) because set-to-empty versus remove is ambiguous. `uid` (immutable) and `password` (use POST /api/users/password) are rejected, as is any unknown key. `cn` and `sn` are required attributes and cannot be removed. At least one field besides `dn` is required.

GroupPatchRequest.description: JSON Merge Patch (RFC 7396) for a group's own attributes; membership has its own endpoints. Absent keys are kept, a non-empty string sets, `null` removes `description`. `cn` cannot be removed. Unknown keys and empty strings are rejected (400). At least one field besides `dn` is required.

BackupJob.description: One backup run. Contains no secrets, no remote output, no paths outside the backup root and no requester DN (only a one-way fingerprint).

status.description: `abandoned`: the controller restarted and no result could be established.

fingerprint.description: 16-hex one-way fingerprint of the requesting identity.

deadline_at.description: Start time plus the per-kind maximum run time.

orphan_suspected.description: The controller restarted while a worker still held the lock; the job stays `running` until that worker ends.

IdempotencyKey.description: Optional retry-safety key (16-128 characters from `[A-Za-z0-9._~:-]`, bare or double-quoted; one header only, otherwise 400). The first request with a key executes; a retry of the same request (same method, route, query and body) replays the first status, body and `Location` with `Idempotent-Replayed: true` and writes nothing again. The key is scoped to the authenticated identity and to the request: a different request under the same key is 422 `idempotency_key_reused`, a request still in flight is 409 `idempotency_key_conflict` (retryable). Only 2xx results, `partial_failure` and `idempotency_outcome_unknown` are stored (24h by default); other failures are not, so the key may be reused. A replay is answered before `If-Match` is evaluated. Where the server does not enable it (`GET /api/server-settings` `idempotencyEnabled`), a key is refused with 422 `idempotency_unsupported`, never silently ignored. Records are kept in process memory (a restart forgets them); a full store refuses new keys with 503 `idempotency_capacity` and `Retry-After`. On `POST /api/users/password` a key is accepted only with an explicit `password` (a generated password would have to be stored). On `POST /api/v1/backups/jobs/{id}` the key is kept in the durable job record instead (same job and 202 on a retry, also after a restart) and needs `UI_IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_FILE`. With a key the request body must be exactly one JSON value (no trailing data, no duplicate or case-colliding field names; none at all on DELETE) of at most 64 KiB, sent as application/json; anything else is 400 `invalid_request` (also for an oversized body: 400, not 413) and does not take the key.

IdempotentReplayed.description: `true` on a response replayed from an Idempotency-Key record; absent on the original response.

x-ai-hints.authFlow: POST /api/login with a cookie jar, then reuse the jar. Check GET /api/v1/meta first for authMode; in sso mode scripted login is not possible.
x-ai-hints.writeSafety: Read before write: fetch the resource, take its ETag (users/groups: the `etag` field or GET /api/entry's ETag header), send it as If-Match. Prefer PATCH over PUT for partial updates: PUT erases optional fields it omits. Set Origin to the server's own origin on profile/backup writes.
neverDo: Do not log or persist generatedPassword
Do not retry destructive operations blindly
Do not assume a truncated list is complete
x-ai-hints.listing: Page GET /api/users and /api/groups with limit (1-200) and the returned nextCursor until hasMore is false, resending the same q; continue on hasMore, not on page length. 422 size_limit_exceeded is never a partial result: narrow with q or use an identity exempt from the directory size limit.
